topics.title: Revision of SS1 & SS2 Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall the fundamental concepts of beauty and cosmetology from SS1 and SS2.
The students should be able to identify different skincare treatments and their purposes.
The students should be able to explain the proper sanitation procedures in a beauty salon.
The students should be able to demonstrate basic hairstyling techniques.

Introduction:
Today we will revise the key concepts you learned in SS1 and SS2 to build a strong foundation for your final year. This revision will help you connect previous knowledge with the advanced topics we will cover this term.

Content:
We will begin by reviewing the core areas of beauty and cosmetology. First, skincare fundamentals: understanding different skin types (normal, dry, oily, combination, sensitive) and appropriate treatments for each. Remember how we identified skin types using the tissue paper test? We also covered facial treatments including cleansing, exfoliation, steaming, extraction, and moisturizing. For Nigerian skin, we must consider our climate and how the harmattan season affects skin hydration.

Next, we will review hair care and styling. This includes understanding hair types (fine, medium, coarse) and textures (straight, wavy, curly, coily). We learned about basic haircuts, shampooing techniques, and conditioning treatments. Special attention was given to natural hair care, which is increasingly popular in Nigeria, including the LOC method (Liquid, Oil, Cream) and protective styling.

Sanitation and safety procedures are crucial in any beauty establishment. We covered proper disinfection of tools and equipment, waste disposal, and client consultation protocols. In Nigerian salon settings, maintaining high standards of hygiene prevents cross-contamination and ensures client safety.

Finally, we will revisit nail care basics, including manicure and pedicure procedures, nail diseases and disorders, and nail art techniques. We discussed how to properly sanitize tools and maintain a clean workstation, which is especially important when working with clients in our busy market environments.

Class activity:
Divide into groups of four. Each group will create a mind map connecting different aspects of beauty and cosmetology from SS1 and SS2. Include at least one practical application for each concept, such as how to perform a basic facial or style natural hair. Be prepared to present your mind maps to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. List the five basic skin types and recommend one appropriate product for each.
2. Explain the proper steps for disinfecting hair cutting scissors.
3. What are the three main sections of a basic shampoo service?
4. How would you adapt a skincare consultation for a client during the harmattan season?
5. Differentiate between a bacterial and fungal nail infection, including one symptom of each.

Summary:
Today's revision has reinforced the foundational knowledge you need as we advance to more specialized topics in beauty and cosmetology this term.

topics.title: Professional Makeup Artistry I
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create a professional makeup portfolio showcasing their best work.
The students should be able to identify and develop their signature makeup style.
The students should be able to apply makeup techniques suitable for different face shapes and skin tones.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper makeup sanitation practices.

Introduction:
Building on our revision of previous knowledge, we now focus on professional makeup artistry, beginning with portfolio development and signature style creation. These skills are essential for establishing yourself as a professional makeup artist in Nigeria's competitive beauty industry.

Content:
A professional makeup portfolio is your visual resume and most powerful marketing tool. Start by selecting your 10-15 strongest makeup looks across different categories: everyday wear, bridal, editorial, and special effects. Photograph each look professionally with good lighting and clear focus on the makeup application. Include before-and-after shots to highlight your transformation skills. For Nigerian clients, ensure your portfolio represents diverse skin tones and features that reflect our population.

Developing your signature style involves identifying your strengths and aesthetic preferences. Do you excel in natural looks, bold colors, or cultural makeup? Study successful Nigerian makeup artists like Banke Meshida or Lola Maja to understand how they've established distinctive styles. Your signature should be recognizable while demonstrating versatility across different client needs and occasions.

Face shape analysis is fundamental in makeup artistry. The common face shapes are oval, round, square, heart, and diamond. For each shape, specific contouring and highlighting techniques accentuate features and create balance. For example, round faces benefit from contouring at the temples and jawline to create definition, while square faces can be softened with highlighter on the forehead and chin. Nigerian facial features often require customized approaches to these standard techniques.

Skin tone matching is another critical skill. Nigerian skin tones range from fair to deep, with warm, cool, or neutral undertones. Learn to identify undertones by examining veins (blue veins indicate cool, green indicate warm) and how skin reacts to sunlight. Select foundation shades that match perfectly, as mismatched foundation is immediately noticeable in our bright Nigerian sunlight and at social events like weddings or owambe gatherings.

Proper sanitation prevents cross-contamination and ensures client safety. Always disinfect brushes and sponges between clients using alcohol-based solutions or brush cleaners. Store makeup properly to maintain consistency and prevent bacterial growth. Never double-dip applicators into products, and use disposable mascara wands and lip liners when possible. In Nigeria's warm climate, makeup products can spoil faster, so proper storage is especially important.

Class activity:
Create a signature makeup look that represents your personal style and works well for Nigerian skin tones. Apply this look on a mannequin or willing partner, focusing on proper technique and sanitation. Photograph your work and write a brief artist statement explaining your inspiration and the techniques used. Be prepared to present your work to the class for feedback.

Evaluation questions:
1. List five essential elements to include in a professional makeup portfolio.
2. Explain how you would contour a square face shape and why this technique is effective.
3. Describe the process for properly disinfecting a makeup brush after use.
4. How would you adapt a makeup look for an outdoor Nigerian wedding versus an indoor corporate event?
5. What considerations should be made when selecting foundation shades for deep Nigerian skin tones?

Summary:
Professional makeup artistry requires technical skill, artistic vision, and business acumen. Developing your signature style and building a strong portfolio are essential steps toward establishing yourself as a makeup artist in Nigeria's beauty industry.

topics.title: Professional Makeup Artistry II
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to apply makeup techniques suitable for high fashion and photography.
The students should be able to create editorial makeup looks for various publications.
The students should be able to adapt makeup applications for different lighting conditions.
The students should be able to collaborate effectively with photographers and creative directors.

Introduction:
Building on our foundation in professional makeup artistry, we now explore specialized applications in high fashion, photography, and editorial work. These advanced techniques will prepare you for the dynamic world of beauty and fashion media in Nigeria and beyond.

Content:
High fashion makeup is characterized by creativity, boldness, and innovation. Unlike everyday wear, high fashion makeup prioritizes artistic expression over practicality. Key techniques include graphic liner, avant-garde color combinations, unconventional placement of products, and the use of unconventional materials. Nigerian high fashion often incorporates cultural elements, such as traditional makeup patterns inspired by Adire fabric or Gele headtie designs. Study international fashion weeks and Nigerian designers like Lisa Folawiyo to understand current high fashion makeup trends.

Photography makeup requires understanding how different cameras and lighting capture makeup details. High-resolution cameras can emphasize texture and imperfection, so skin preparation must be meticulous. Photography makeup typically involves heavier application than everyday wear to ensure it reads clearly on camera. For outdoor Nigerian photoshoots, consider the harsh sunlight and how it affects makeup longevity. Products with long-wear formulations and setting sprays are essential to prevent melting and fading.

Editorial makeup tells a story and complements the overall theme of a publication. Whether for a magazine, lookbook, or online content, editorial makeup aligns with the creative direction of the photoshoot. Research Nigerian publications like TW Magazine or Genevieve Magazine to understand the editorial makeup aesthetic. Editorial looks often trend bolder than everyday wear but remain cohesive with the fashion and styling elements. Collaboration with the photographer, stylist, and creative director ensures the makeup enhances the overall vision.

Lighting adaptation is crucial for professional makeup artists. Natural daylight, fluorescent lighting, studio lights, and candlelight all affect how makeup appears. In Nigeria, we often work with bright natural light that can reveal undertones and texture. Practice applying makeup in different lighting conditions to understand how colors shift and how products perform. For evening events or indoor venues with dim lighting, consider stronger pigments and more defined features to ensure the makeup remains visible.

Working with photographers requires clear communication and understanding of technical aspects. Discuss the camera equipment, shooting location, and desired mood beforehand. Be prepared to make adjustments during the shoot based on feedback. Nigerian fashion photography often happens in diverse locations, from urban Lagos streets to natural outdoor settings, so adaptability is key. Building strong professional relationships with photographers can lead to ongoing work opportunities.

Class activity:
Working in pairs, create an editorial makeup look based on a Nigerian cultural theme. One student will apply the makeup while the other will act as photographer. Consider how the makeup will translate in photographs and adjust techniques accordingly. Document your process and final results with photographs, and be prepared to present your concept and execution to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. Explain three key differences between high fashion makeup and everyday wear makeup.
2. How would you adapt a makeup look for an outdoor photoshoot in direct Nigerian sunlight versus an indoor studio shoot with artificial lighting?
3. Describe the process of collaborating with a photographer on a fashion editorial shoot.
4. What cultural elements might you incorporate into a high fashion makeup look inspired by Nigerian heritage?
5. Why is skin preparation particularly important for photography makeup, and what steps would you take to ensure flawless skin appearance on camera?

Summary:
High fashion, photography, and editorial makeup represent the artistic pinnacle of makeup artistry, requiring technical expertise, creative vision, and adaptability to various environments and client needs.

topics.title: Bridal and Event Management in Beauty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to coordinate complete bridal looks for different cultural weddings.
The students should be able to plan and execute beauty services for various events.
The students should be able to manage client consultations and expectations effectively.
The students should be able to organize a team of beauty professionals for large events.

Introduction:
As we progress in our beauty and cosmetology studies, we now focus on bridal and event management-specialized services that require coordination, planning, and client management skills. These are lucrative aspects of the beauty industry in Nigeria, where weddings and social events are significant occasions.

Content:
Bridal makeup and hairstyling require careful planning and execution. Begin with thorough consultations to understand the bride's vision, cultural background, and wedding theme. Nigerian weddings often blend traditional and modern elements, so research specific customs like the traditional engagement (Igba Nkwu), church ceremony, and reception. Create a timeline for the wedding day, accounting for multiple looks if needed. Pack a comprehensive emergency kit with products to address any issues that may arise, such as foundation shade matches for different lighting or products to control shine in our humid climate.

Cultural considerations are essential in Nigerian bridal beauty. For Igbo weddings, consider the traditional red and white makeup palette and Gele styling. For Yoruba weddings, gold and coral accessories often complement the makeup. Hausa brides may prefer more conservative looks with subtle makeup and elegant hijab styling. Understanding these cultural nuances demonstrates respect and ensures the bride feels authentic on her special day. Always ask about specific cultural requirements during consultations to avoid misunderstandings.

Event management in beauty extends beyond weddings to include birthdays, anniversaries, corporate events, and owambe parties. Each event has unique requirements regarding timing, location, and client needs. For outdoor events in Nigeria's heat, prioritize long-wear, waterproof products and setting sprays. For corporate events, maintain a professional appearance with natural makeup and elegant hairstyles. Create detailed schedules for beauty teams, ensuring services are delivered efficiently without keeping guests waiting.

Client consultation skills are vital for successful bridal and event beauty services. Ask open-ended questions to understand the client's vision, preferences, and concerns. Show portfolio examples of similar work to manage expectations. Discuss pricing packages, payment schedules, and cancellation policies clearly. In Nigeria's economic climate, be transparent about additional costs for products or travel to avoid disputes. Follow up consultations with written confirmations detailing all agreed-upon services.

Team coordination is essential for large events involving multiple beauty professionals. Assign specific roles based on each team member's strengths-some may excel in makeup, others in hairstyling or nail services. Conduct pre-event briefings to ensure everyone understands the timeline and client requirements. For Nigerian weddings with multiple bridesmaids, consider creating a team WhatsApp group for real-time communication on the wedding day. Always have a contingency plan for no-shows or emergencies.

Class activity:
Plan a complete beauty package for a Nigerian traditional wedding. Include consultations for the bride and bridal party, makeup and hair options for different wedding events, and a detailed timeline for the wedding day. Consider cultural elements, weather factors, and budget considerations. Present your package to the class, explaining your decisions and how you would handle potential challenges.

Evaluation questions:
1. List five essential items to include in a bridal beauty emergency kit for a Nigerian wedding.
2. Explain how you would adapt a bridal makeup look for an outdoor wedding during the harmattan season versus a rainy season wedding.
3. Describe the process of conducting an effective consultation with a bride for her traditional wedding makeup.
4. What cultural considerations should be made when providing beauty services for an Igbo traditional wedding versus a Yoruba traditional wedding?
5. How would you coordinate a team of five beauty professionals for a wedding with 20 bridesmaids and ensure everyone is ready on time?

Summary:
Successful bridal and event management in beauty requires cultural sensitivity, meticulous planning, and excellent client communication skills to create memorable experiences for clients during their special occasions.

topics.title: Midterm Test
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate their understanding of professional makeup artistry concepts.
The students should be able to apply knowledge of bridal and event management principles.
The students should be able to identify and explain key sanitation and safety procedures in beauty services.

Introduction:
Today's midterm test will assess your understanding of the concepts we've covered this term, including professional makeup artistry and bridal and event management. This evaluation will help me gauge your progress and identify areas that need additional focus before we continue with the remaining topics.

Content:
The midterm test will cover all topics we've studied this term, with emphasis on professional makeup artistry (weeks 2-3) and bridal and event management (week 4). You will be tested on both theoretical knowledge and practical application of concepts.

For the professional makeup artistry section, expect questions about portfolio development, signature style creation, face shape analysis, skin tone matching, and high fashion techniques. You should be able to explain how to adapt makeup for different lighting conditions and photography needs. Questions may include identifying appropriate products for different skin types and explaining sanitation procedures for makeup tools.

The bridal and event management section will test your knowledge of consultation techniques, cultural considerations for Nigerian weddings, event planning, and team coordination. You should be able to create detailed timelines for wedding days and identify essential items for a bridal emergency kit. Questions may ask you to compare different cultural wedding traditions and their beauty requirements.

The test will consist of multiple choice, short answer, and practical application questions. You will also be asked to create a sample consultation form and outline a bridal beauty package for a specific Nigerian wedding type. Remember to demonstrate your understanding of how Nigerian climate and cultural factors influence beauty services.

Class activity:
The midterm test will be administered during this class period. Please arrive on time with all necessary writing materials. The test will take approximately 90 minutes to complete. After completing the test, you may begin reading ahead on the next topic: Cosmetology Entrepreneurship Project.

Evaluation questions:
The midterm test will serve as the evaluation for this week, with questions covering all topics studied this term.

Summary:
Today's midterm test provides an opportunity to demonstrate your knowledge and understanding of the beauty and cosmetology concepts we've covered this term. Your results will help guide our continued learning journey.

topics.title: Cosmetology Entrepreneurship Project I
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the importance of proposal writing in cosmetology business.
The students should be able to list the essential components of a business proposal.
The students should be able to conduct a basic market survey for a cosmetology business.
The students should be able to differentiate between primary and secondary market research methods.

Introduction:
In our previous lessons, we have learned about various beauty treatments and techniques. Today, we will explore how to turn these skills into a successful business venture by learning about proposal writing and market survey, which are crucial first steps in entrepreneurship.

Content:
Proposal Writing:
A business proposal is a document that outlines the plan for a new business or project. In cosmetology, it serves as a blueprint for your beauty salon, spa, or makeup artist business. The proposal should include:
1. Executive Summary: A brief overview of your business concept, mission statement, and objectives. For example, "Beauty Haven Salon aims to provide affordable and high-quality beauty services to residents of Lagos Island."
2. Business Description: Details about your business, including the type of services you'll offer (hair styling, makeup, skincare, nail art, etc.), your unique selling proposition, and business structure.
3. Market Analysis: Information about your target market, competitors, and industry trends. For instance, identifying that there's a growing demand for natural hair care services in Abuja.
4. Organization and Management: Outline of your business structure, management team, and staffing needs.
5. Services Offered: Detailed description of the beauty services you'll provide, pricing structure, and any specialized treatments.
6. Marketing and Sales Strategy: How you'll attract customers, promote your services, and retain clients.
7. Financial Projections: Startup costs, revenue forecasts, and break-even analysis. For example, calculating the cost of equipment like hairdryers, styling chairs, and makeup supplies.

Market Survey:
A market survey is a systematic gathering and analysis of information about the market for your beauty services. It helps you understand customer needs, preferences, and the competitive landscape. Types of market research:
1. Primary Research: Original research you conduct yourself.
 - Surveys: Questionnaires distributed to potential customers. For example, asking women in Enugu about their preferred beauty treatments.
 - Interviews: One-on-one discussions with potential clients.
 - Focus Groups: Group discussions with target customers.
2. Secondary Research: Information collected by others.
 - Industry reports: Studies on the beauty industry in Nigeria.
 - Competitor analysis: Researching existing salons in your area.
 - Government statistics: Data on population demographics and income levels.

Steps to conduct a market survey:
1. Define your objectives: Determine what information you need (e.g., pricing expectations, service preferences).
2. Identify your target audience: Who are your potential customers? (e.g., young professionals, students, elderly women).
3. Choose your research methods: Will you use online surveys, face-to-face interviews, or a combination?
4. Design your research instrument: Create clear, unbiased questions for your survey or interview guide.
5. Collect data: Implement your survey or conduct interviews.
6. Analyze findings: Look for patterns, trends, and insights.
7. Make decisions: Use the information to refine your business plan.

Class Activity:
Students will work in groups of 4-5 to develop a business proposal for a new beauty salon in their local area. Each group will conduct a mock market survey by interviewing at least 10 potential customers (classmates can role-play) about their beauty service preferences, price sensitivity, and expectations. Groups will present their findings and proposal outline to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the seven essential components of a cosmetology business proposal?
2. Differentiate between primary and secondary market research methods with examples relevant to a beauty business.
3. Why is market research crucial before starting a beauty salon business in Nigeria?
4. List three specific questions you would include in a market survey for a new makeup artist business targeting university students.
5. How might the harmattan season affect your beauty business operations, and how would your proposal address this challenge?

Summary:
Effective proposal writing and thorough market research are fundamental steps in establishing a successful cosmetology business in Nigeria's competitive beauty industry.

topics.title: Midterm Break
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
Students should be able to identify the importance of midterm breaks in academic performance.
Students should be able to explain how to effectively utilize midterm breaks for personal development.
Introduction:
As we conclude the first half of the term, it is essential to recognize the value of midterm breaks in maintaining academic excellence and personal well-being. This break provides an opportunity for students to rest and prepare for the remaining weeks of the term.
Content:
Midterm breaks serve as crucial periods for students to recharge both mentally and physically. During this time, students should engage in activities that promote relaxation and skill development. For beauty and cosmetology students, this could involve practicing new techniques learned in previous weeks, researching current trends in the beauty industry, or observing professional cosmetologists at local salons. The break also allows students to reflect on their academic progress so far and identify areas that need improvement before the second half of the term begins. Additionally, students can use this time to prepare for upcoming assessments and practical demonstrations that will form part of their final evaluation.
Class activity:
Students are encouraged to maintain a beauty journal during the midterm break, documenting any new techniques they learn, beauty trends they observe, or personal reflections on their academic journey so far. They should also identify one area of beauty and cosmetology they wish to improve upon during the break and set specific goals for skill development.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is the primary purpose of a midterm break in an academic setting?
2. How can beauty and cosmetology students utilize their midterm break for professional development?
3. Identify three activities a cosmetology student might engage in during the midterm break to enhance their skills.
4. Explain how taking a break can actually improve academic performance in practical subjects like beauty and cosmetology.
Summary:
Midterm breaks are essential for academic rejuvenation and professional development in beauty and cosmetology, providing students with the opportunity to rest, reflect, and enhance their technical skills before continuing with the term's curriculum.
